title: A combined protocol for isolation of T6SS-positive Campylobacter jejuni and assessment of interspecies interaction
protocol: Place freshly collected fecal contents from broiler chickens in sterile 1× PBS (pH 7.4).
Keep samples on ice and process immediately.
Humanely kill the chickens according to approved animal ethics protocol.
Lay the chicken on its back on tissue paper.
Clean the surface of the chicken thoroughly with 70% ethanol.
Pin the sacrificed chicken down to secure it to a tray at the wings, shoulders, and legs.
Remove the skin of the chicken starting from the lower abdomen to the top of the thorax to expose the digestive tract.
Cut the cecum pair and gently place it in a sterile petri-plate.
Clean the outer surface of the cecum using a sterile scalpel to remove mucous or blood clots.
Cut the cecum longitudinally.
Use a sterile scalpel to scrape and rub the inner epithelial surface of the cecum.
Take the cecal content into a sterile micro-centrifuge tube.
Suspend 500 mg cecal content in 1 ml of sterile 1× PBS.
Mix the cecum content by vortexing for 10 min to make a homogenous mixture.
Dilute homogenized samples up to 10-3 in Mueller Hinton broth.
Inoculate 100 μL of the sample from the 10-3 dilution onto Blood Free Campylobacter Selectivity Agar Base media supplemented with CAT Selective Supplement.
Incubate the agar plates at 42°C for 48 hours under microaerophilic conditions.
Prepare a soft agar plate for bacterial motility assessment.
Spot inoculate a single colony onto the prepared soft agar plate.
Incubate the plate for 24-48 hours at appropriate conditions.
Measure the diameter of the hollow formation around the colonies to assess swarming ability.
Pick an individual colony and add it into a 4% H2O2 solution for catalase test.
Observe typical bubble formation in H2O2 solution as an indicator of catalase presence specific to Campylobacter sp.
Add bacterial inoculum to a blotting paper soaked with oxidase solution.
Check if the inoculated area turns blue, indicating cytochrome c oxidase production by Campylobacter sp.
Incubate an individual colony in 1% Hippurate solution for hippurate hydrolysis test.
Overlay ninhydrin solution on top of the incubated Hippurate solution.
Observe appearance of purple color as confirmation of hippuricase enzyme specific to C. jejuni.
Examine colonies on selective media for size, shape, elevation, color, surface type, and odor.
Perform Gram staining procedure for morphological characterization.
Use Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FESEM) for detailed bacterial morphology analysis.
Take bacterial samples from an overnight grown culture and prepare a smear on a glass slide.
Air-dry cell smear.
Heat fix the slide by passing it over a flame several times.
Flood the dried smear with crystal violet staining reagent for 1 min.
Discard the flooded crystal violet stain and wash the slide under a slow stream of tap water for 5 s.
Cover the smear with Gram’s iodine and wait for 1 min.
Discard the residual Gram’s iodine and wash the slide under a slow stream of tap water for 5 s.
Add decolorizing agent (95% ethanol) and keep it for 15 s.
Rinse the slide under a slow stream of water for 10 s.
After completely drying, flood the slide with safranin counterstain and wait for another 30 s.
Wash the slide under a slow stream of tap water until no color appears in the effluent.
Observe the results under oil immersion using a brightfield microscope with a magnification of 60×.
Take the bacterial culture and adjust the OD600 to approximately 0.6 by adding fresh medium.
Centrifuge 1 mL of the culture at 5,000 × g for 6 minutes at room temperature (approximately 25°C).
Resuspend the cells in 300 μL of 1× PBS and centrifuge again at 5,000 × g for 6 minutes.
Repeat the resuspension and centrifugation steps two more times with 1× PBS.
Add 300 μL of 2.5% (v/v) glutaraldehyde to fix the cells and incubate at room temperature for 1 hour.
Centrifuge the fixed cells at 5,000 × g for 6 minutes.
Wash the cell pellet three times with 300 μL of 1× PBS for 10 minutes each.
Resuspend the cells in 300 μL of 35% ethanol and incubate for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Dehydrate fixed cells sequentially in 50%, 70%, and 95% ethanol.
Resuspend dehydrated cells using 500 μL of 100% ethanol.
Incubate resuspended cells for 1 hour to complete dehydration.
Cast 10 μL of the sample on a cover slip or silicon wafer.
Dry the cover slip at room temperature (approximately 25°C) for 2 hours.
Vacuum-dry fixed and dehydrated samples for 1 hour.
Fix samples to aluminum stubs.
Coat samples with platinum using a coating instrument.
Capture images of platinum-coated samples using the secondary electron detector under high vacuum conditions.
Use magnifications ranging from 3,000× to 20,000× during imaging.
Pour 0.4% Mueller Hinton Agar into each well of a 6-well tissue culture plate.
Adjust the absorbance (OD600) of the bacterial culture to 1.00.
Inoculate 5 μL of the adjusted culture as a spot in the center of the agar and let it dry.
Incubate the inoculated plate for 24 h at 42°C under micro-aerophilic conditions.
Measure the diameter of the spread zone with a ruler throughout the area of growth around the central point of the plate.
Incubate bacteria in microaerophilic conditions (85% N2, 10% CO2, and 5% O2) at 37°C for 18-24 hours.
Perform catalase test on the bacterial culture.
Perform oxidase test on the bacterial culture.
Perform hippurate hydrolysis test on the bacterial culture.
Mix bacterial inoculum with hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) solution.
Place a microscope slide inside a petri dish.
Keep the petri dish cover available.
Collect a small amount of well-isolated colony using a sterile inoculating loop or wooden stick and place it onto the microscope slide.
Immediately cover the petri dish with a lid to limit aerosols.
Observe immediate bubble formation against a dark background.
Centrifuge 1 mL of well-grown culture at 6,000 × g for 5 min and decant the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of 1× PBS.
Add 150 μL of 30% H2O2 solution to the resuspended cells.
Observe bubble formation against a dark background.
Soak a small filter paper in an oxidase reagent and let it dry.
Pick a well-isolated colony from a fresh bacterial plate using a loop, rub it onto treated filter paper, and wait for 10–15 min.
Observe the filter paper for color changes to blue, indicating oxidase-positive.
Suspend a loop full of well-isolated colonies from a fresh bacterial plate in 5 mL MH broth.
Grow the culture for 18–24 hours (OD600∼0.6) at 37°C in microaerophilic conditions.
Centrifuge the grown culture at 5,000 × g for 6 minutes and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL 1× PBS (pH∼7.4).
Centrifuge the suspension at 5,000 × g for 6 minutes.
Repeat the washing step three times.
Discard the supernatant after each wash.
Add 400 μL of 1%-hippurate solution to the mixture.
Incubate the mixture at 37°C for 2 hours.
Slowly add 200 μL of the 3.5%-ninhydrin solution to the side of the tube.
Re-incubate the mixture at 37°C for 20 minutes.
Observe the formation of a purple color.
Centrifuge 5 mL of well-grown C. jejuni culture (16-18 hours, OD600 ∼ 0.6) at 10,000 × g for 3 minutes.
Resuspend the pellet in 200 μL of lysis buffer.
Mix vigorously by pipetting.
Incubate the solution at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Add 80 μL of 5 M NaCl solution and mix well.
Centrifuge the viscous solution at 10,000 × g for 8 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the clear supernatant into a new micro-centrifuge tube.
Add 200 μL of chloroform. Perform this step in the fume hood due to the volatile nature of chloroform.
Invert the solution at least 80 times or rotate the tube on a spinning wheel for at least 1 minute to form a milky solution.
Centrifuge it at 10,000 × g for 3 minutes.
Pipette the supernatant into a new vial without touching the second layer.
Add 150 μL of 100% molecular grade ethanol and tap the tube gently to mix properly.
Centrifuge it at 10,000 × g for 5 minutes and decant the supernatant.
Add 150 μL of 70% ethanol and tap the tube gently to mix properly.
Centrifuge it at 10,000 × g for 5 minutes and decant the supernatant.
Repeat steps xiii–xiv twice.
Dry the pellet inside a laminar air-flow for 15 minutes to minimize ethanol contamination.
Dissolve the pellet with 30 μL TE buffer.
Perform 16S rRNA gene sequencing to identify bacteria at the species level.
Amplify 16S rRNA and hcp genes using PCR with specific primers.
Purify PCR products using a PCR purification kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Subject purified PCR products to Sanger sequencing for sequence determination.
Construct a phylogenetic tree from hcp gene sequences to determine relatedness among T6SS positive C. jejuni and other Gram-negative bacteria harboring T6SS.
Perform BLAST analysis of the DNA sequence.
Open the histogram of Sanger sequencing data and copy the nucleotide sequence.
Go to the NCBI website and open Nucleotide BLAST.
Paste the copied sequence into the BLAST search field.
Click on the BLAST option to perform the analysis.
Download sequences of C. jejuni 16S rRNA gene from NCBI in FASTA format.
Create a text file and merge all downloaded sequences including the isolate sequence.
Open MEGA X software and go to File, then open the merged text file.
In MEGA X, select Align and choose New Alignment option.
Select DNA as the alignment type and choose the text file containing the sequences.
Export the generated alignment in MEGA format.
From the Phylogeny menu in MEGA X, select Maximum Likelihood Tree method.
Construct the phylogenetic tree using the exported alignment data.
Prepare 1 mL of 25% bacterial glycerol stock by mixing 500 μL MH broth and 500 μL 50% glycerol, then store at -80°C.
Reduce the final volume up to 100 μL for single-use glycerol stock (50 μL MH broth and 50 μL 50% glycerol), then store at -80°C.
Take single-use glycerol stocks of C. jejuni isolates.
Grow them on MH plates overnight at 42°C under microaerophilic conditions.
Inoculate bacterial cells from the MH plate into MH broth.
Incubate the culture overnight under continuous shaking conditions (42°C, microaerophilic).
Adjust the absorbance of the culture to OD600 = 0.3 by dilution with MH broth.
Add 1 mL of C. jejuni culture to wells of a 24-well cell culture plate.
Incubate at 42°C under microaerophilic conditions for 24 hours.
Remove planktonic cells using a pipette.
Wash remaining biofilm with 500 μL of 1× PBS.
Add 1 mL of 0.1% (w/v) Crystal Violet staining solution.
Incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature (∼25°C).
Remove unbound dye and wash plate three times with 1× PBS.
Allow the plate to dry.
Dissolve bound dye in 30% glacial acetic acid.
Incubate for 15 min at room temperature (∼25°C).
Measure the absorbance at 595 nm using a microplate reader.
Open Gen5 software and select the 'New' option.
Choose the 'Plate type', 'Read' option, 'Absorbance', 'Endpoint', and 'Monochromators'.
Set the wavelength according to experimental purposes.
Select the ‘Read’ option in the software.
Click on ‘OK’ in the temperature dialogue box.
Prepare bacterial biofilm on a coverslip in a 35 mm petri plate.
Wash the coverslip as mentioned earlier.
Add 0.005% acridine orange to the coverslip and wait for 5 min.
Thoroughly wash the stain with 500 μL of 1× PBS thrice.
Mount the coverslips using 5 μL Vecta-shield mounting media for imaging.
Visualize acridine orange-stained biofilm using a FITC filter with an excitation wavelength of 400–520 nm and an emission wavelength of 480–580 nm.
Conduct Western blot analysis on TCA precipitated protein from C. jejuni using an anti-Hcp polyclonal antibody.
Probe the supernatant (in serial dilution) from C. jejuni with an anti-Hcp polyclonal antibody for indirect ELISA.
Incubate the plates with HRP-conjugated goat anti-rabbit IgG secondary antibody after probing.
Develop the plates with TMB substrate and measure absorbance at 450 nm in a UV-VIS multi-plate reader.
Ice-chill the bacterial culture supernatant before adding TCA to prevent protein degradation.
Precipitate proteins by adding trichloroacetic acid (TCA) to the ice-chilled supernatant.
Wash the precipitated pellet with acetone, then air-dry it completely.
Transfer the dried pellet into a clean tube and dissolve in sample buffer for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Charge PVDF membrane with 100% methanol before use.
Wash the charged PVDF membrane with transfer buffer.
Place the prepared PVDF membrane on top of the polyacrylamide gel.
Adjust the absorbance (OD600) of a freshly grown T6SS+ve C. jejuni culture to 1.00 in 500 mL.
Centrifuge the culture at 6,000 × g for 8 minutes at 4°C.
Chill the supernatant on ice for 30 minutes.
Add 15% TCA to the supernatant and keep it on ice for 90 to 120 minutes.
Centrifuge the TCA-mixed supernatant at 5,000 × g for 20 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in ice-chilled acetone.
Centrifuge the acetone suspension at 5,000 × g for 20 minutes at 4°C.
Dry the pellet in air for 15 to 30 minutes.
Add 50 μL of 1× Laemmli buffer to the dried pellet.
Run the sample on a 15% SDS-PAGE gel.
Mix reagents to prepare resolving gel according to Table 3, adding TEMED last.
Pour the resolving gel solution between two glass plates fixed in an SDS-PAGE casting cassette.
Fill the space above the resolving gel with isopropanol to avoid bubble formation.
Wait for 15 minutes until the resolving gel solidifies.
Mix reagents to prepare stacking gel according to Table 3, adding TEMED last.
Discard the isopropanol and pour the stacking gel solution into the glass plates.
Place the comb accordingly after pouring the stacking gel.
Wait for 15 minutes until the stacking gel solidifies.
Place the gel in the running cassette with wells facing inward.
Insert the running cassette with the gel into the running tank.
Fill the gel running tank with 1× SDS-running buffer.
Remove the comb from the gel.
Mix 15 μL of the sample prepared with 1× Laemmli buffer with 4 μL of 5× sample loading dye.
Load the mixture inside the wells.
Set the voltage to 90 volts and run the gel until the dye front comes out.
Cut the gel according to its size.
Place the gel in 1× transfer buffer (in shaking condition) for 10 minutes at room temperature (∼25°C).
Charge the PVDF membrane with methanol for 2 minutes at room temperature (∼25°C).
Discard the methanol and wash the PVDF membrane with 1× transfer buffer for 15 minutes at room temperature (∼25°C).
Soak filter papers and sponges in 1× transfer buffer for 10 minutes at room temperature (∼25°C).
Assemble a ‘sandwich’ of gel and PVDF membrane.
Roll a small glass rod over the ‘sandwich’ to prevent any bubble formation between the gel and the membrane.
Fix the transfer cassette into the transfer chamber.
Run the transfer procedure at 90 volts for 65 minutes in a 4°C environment.
Take out the PVDF membrane from the Western blot cassette after transfer completion.
Dip the membrane into blocking buffer and incubate overnight (∼12 hours) at 4°C.
Wash the membrane twice with TBST solution and three times with TBS at room temperature (∼25°C).
Add anti-Hcp primary antibody (1:5,000 dilution) and incubate at room temperature for 1 h.
Wash the membrane twice with TBST solution and three times with TBS at room temperature.
Add Goat anti-rabbit HRP conjugated IgG (H+L) secondary antibody (1:3,500 dilution) and incubate at room temperature for 1 h.
Wash the membrane two times with TBST solution and three times with TBS.
Add 10 mL DAB color developing solution and keep in the dark for 5 min.
Observe for brown precipitate formation at the corresponding size of Hcp (∼20 kDa).
Take the freshly grown culture of T6SS+ve C. jejuni and adjust the OD600 to 1.
Centrifuge the culture at 5,000 × g for 5 min and take the culture supernatant.
Coat the 96-well ELISA plates with bacterial culture supernatant serially diluted (two-fold) in carbonate-bicarbonate buffer (pH ∼9.6).
Use the micropipette to dispense 100 μL of carbonate-bicarbonate buffer (pH∼9.6) to the second, third, and fourth well.
Use the micropipette to transfer 200 μL of the test sample (undiluted bacterial culture supernatant) to the first well.
Use the micropipette to mix the test sample (undiluted bacterial culture supernatant) in the well.
Draw up 100 μL of the supernatant and dispense it to the second well (to make a 1:2 dilution).
Mix the solution by pipetting.
Draw up 100 μL of the supernatant from the second well, and dispense it to the third well (to make a 1:4 dilution in the third well).
Mix it thoroughly by pipetting.
Draw up 100 μL of the diluted supernatant from the third well, and expel it in the fourth well (to make a 1:8 dilution).
Use the micropipette to mix it by pipetting.
Discard 100 μL of the diluted supernatant from the fourth well.
Incubate the plate overnight (∼12 h) at 4°C.
Remove the coated sample and wash the wells thrice with 100 μL of PBS-T/well.
Discard the content by tapping the inverted plate on absorbent material such as tissue paper.
After washing, add 100 μL of 5% blocking solution to each well.
Incubate for 1 h at 37°C.
Wash the plate thrice with 100 μL of PBS-T per well.
Probe with rabbit polyclonal anti-Hcp hyper-immune sera (1:2,000 dilution) in each well for 2 hours at room temperature.
Wash the plate thrice with 100 μL of PBS-T per well.
Add 100 μL HRP-conjugated goat anti-rabbit IgG (H+L) secondary antibody (1:3,500 dilution) in each well and incubate for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash the plate thrice with 100 μL of PBS-T per well.
Add 100 μL of 1× TMB substrate to develop the reaction.
Stop the color development by adding a stopping solution.
Read the absorbance at 450 nm in a microplate reader.
Generate GFP-expressing E. coli for differentiating competing bacteria during inter-bacterial interaction.
Prepare chemically competent E. coli (DH5α) cells and store them at -80°C.
Take out E. coli (DH5α) competent cell vial from -80°C.
Thaw the competent cell vial in ice for 10 min.
Add 300 ng of pTurbo GFP-B plasmid DNA to the competent cells.
Gently tap the tube 2–3 times to mix.
Place the vial back into ice for 30 min.
Set the heat-block temperature to 42°C.
Incubate the vial in the heat block for 45 s.
Immediately chill the vial on ice for 10 min after heat shock.
Add 1 mL of LB media to the vial and incubate at 37°C with shaking (180 rpm) for 1 h.
Centrifuge the vial at 5,000 × g for 5 min and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 100 μL of fresh LB medium.
Plate the resuspended cells on an LB agar plate containing Ampicillin (100 μg/mL).
Incubate the plates overnight (∼14 h) at 37°C.
Pick green colonies from the agar plate for further study.
Reconstitute chemically competent E. coli (DH5α) cells with p-Turbo-GFP-B plasmid.
Incubate the transformed E. coli cells on LB agar plates.
Visualize GFP expression in recombinant E. coli cells under a microscope equipped with an ApoTome module.
Mix C. jejuni and E. coli cultures for co-incubation.
Co-incubate mixed bacterial cultures for 10 hours.
Wash the co-cultured bacteria after incubation.
Dilute the washed bacteria serially to quantify bacterial colonies.
Count GFP-expressing E. coli colonies on LB agar plates.
Count C. jejuni colonies on LB agar plates.
Fit colony count data with a mathematical model.
Determine birth rates of E. coli and C. jejuni from model fitting.
Determine predation rate (α) from model fitting.
Wash cells in co-culture.
Process cells for epifluorescence microscopy.
Observe cells under an Axio observer microscope equipped with an ApoTome module (Objective magnification: 60×; Scale bar: 5 μm).
Incubate cells on MH agar plate containing bile salt.
Wash cells with PBS.
Treat cells with H2DCFDA for 45 min.
Process cells for epifluorescence microscopy after treatment.
Analyze differential expression of competing bacterial genes by semi-quantitative RT-PCR.
Perform transcriptional profiling of cytokinesis gene (ftsz).
Visualize constitutive expression of GFP in E. coli using epifluorescence microscopy.
Select the green colony and resuspend it in 200 μL 1× PBS.
Centrifuge the resuspended cells at 6,000 × g for 5 min and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 100 μL of 4% paraformaldehyde for fixation.
Incubate the fixed cells for 20 min at room temperature (∼25°C).
Harvest the cells by centrifugation (6,000 × g; 5 min).
Wash the cells twice with 100 μL 1× PBS.
Resuspend the washed cells in 100 μL 1× PBS.
Take a 6 μL aliquot from the sample and make a smear on a grease-free glass slide.
Mount the coverslips using 5 μL Vecta-shield mounting media for imaging.
Mix 1 mL GFP-E. coli culture (6×10^7 CFU/mL) with 1 mL T6SS+ve C. jejuni (6×10^8 CFU/mL).
Add fresh MH broth to the mixture to a total volume of 5 mL.
Incubate the mixture at 37°C under micro-aerophilic conditions for 10 hours.
Perform a serial ten-fold dilution of the co-culture up to a dilution of 10^-5.
Take a 50 μL aliquot from the last dilution and plate it on an MH agar plate containing X-gal (40 μg/mL) and IPTG (0.1 mM).
Incubate the plate at 37°C under micro-aerophilic conditions for 16 hours.
Count the colonies to assess inter-bacterial interaction.
Harvest 2 mL of co-culture by centrifugation at 5,000 × g for 5 minutes after 10 hours.
Wash the cell pellet with 200 μL of 1× PBS.
Centrifuge at 5,000 × g for 5 minutes to discard the supernatant.
Repeat washing and centrifugation steps two more times.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 100 μL of 4% paraformaldehyde.
Incubate at room temperature (∼25°C) for 20 minutes.
Wash the cell pellet with 200 μL of 1× PBS.
Centrifuge at 5,000 × g for 5 minutes to discard the supernatant.
Repeat washing and centrifugation steps two more times.
Resuspend the washed cells in 500 μL of 1× PBS.
Mix 1 mL of GFP-E. coli culture with 1 mL T6SS+ve C. jejuni and 1 mL T6SS-ve C. jejuni.
Make the volume up to 5 mL by adding fresh MH broth.
Incubate the mixture at 37°C in micro-aerophilic conditions for 10 hours.
Centrifuge the bacteria at 5,000 × g for 5 minutes.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 300 μL of Trizol reagent and incubate at room temperature (∼25°C) for 20–30 minutes.
Add 150 μL of molecular biology grade chloroform to the resuspended cells and shake vigorously until the solution turns milky.
Incubate the mixture straight up at room temperature (∼25°C) for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge the Trizol-chloroform mix at 10,000 × g for 25 minutes at 4°C.
Gently pipette out and transfer the upper yellow transparent layer to another microcentrifuge tube.
Add equal volume molecular biology grade isopropanol to the solution.
Keep the solution at −20°C for 12 hours.
Centrifuge the vial at 12,000 × g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the RNA pellet into 100 μL of 70% ethanol.
Centrifuge the suspension at 12,000 × g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the RNA pellet into 50 μL of nuclease-free water.
Take the RNA concentration in nanodrop.
Prepare first-strand cDNA from the RNA sample using Bio-Bharati MuLV Super-transcriptase Kit by following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Amplify the E. coli 16S rRNA gene from the cDNA using a gene-specific primer set and PCR conditions as per the provided protocol tables.
Use No-RT control (cDNA preparation without reverse transcriptase enzyme) to ensure no genomic DNA contamination in the sample.
Validate PCR amplification of the gene of interest using genomic DNA as a positive control and a no-template PCR mixture as a negative control.
Run equal volume of the PCR product on 1% agarose gel.
Open ImageLab software and import the gel image.
Click on the ‘Lane and Band’ option in ImageLab software.
Select the manual option and choose the number of required lanes.
Adjust the box to cover the entire band of interest and click on adjust the frame and resize the frame.
Detect bands and after detection, click on the ‘Report’ option to get the intensity profile of the respective bands.
Use the ‘Total Lane Volume of Intensity’ obtained from the report option to normalize and compare between bands of interest.
Amplify the ftsZ gene using an equal volume of DNA that has been used for amplification of housekeeping gene (16S rRNA).
Co-culture C. jejuni and E. coli in the absence or presence of bile salt (mixture of 50% sodium cholate and 50% sodium deoxycholate, w/w).
Dilute the co-cultured bacterial mixture up to 10-4 dilutions.
Inoculate 100 μL onto an MH agar plate containing bile salt (0.1%, w/v).
Collect colonies from the MH agar plate and resuspend them in 1× PBS to achieve an OD600 of approximately 0.5.
Incubate bacteria with H2DCFDA (20 μM) for 45 min at 37°C.
Centrifuge bacterial cell suspension at 8,000 × g for 2 min.
Resuspend the bacterial pellet in 1× PBS.
Measure fluorescence intensity using a multi-detection microplate reader with excitation filter set to 485 nm and emission filter set to 535 nm.
Incubate cells with H2DCFDA.
Mount 4 μL of cell suspension onto a glass slide using 2 μL of Vecta-shield mounting media.
Observe ROS production in bacterial cells under epifluorescence microscopy with FITC filter (excitation wavelength: 400–520 nm, emission wavelength: 480–580 nm).
Process images in Zen software.
Grow monolayer of human INT407 cells in 24-well tissue culture plate (3×10^5 cells/well).
Add C. jejuni at MOI of 300:1 when the cells become >70% confluent.
Incubate for 3 h at 5% CO2 and 37°C in DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS (Do not add any antibiotics at this stage).
Remove the culture medium and wash the cells with 300 μL/well of 1× PBS two times.
Treat the cells with 500 μL of gentamicin (150 μg/mL) for an additional 2 h.
Wash the cells with 300 μL/well of 1× PBS twice after gentamicin treatment.
Add 200 μL/well of 1% Triton X-100 to lyse cells.
Transfer the suspension into a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Serially dilute (10-fold) the suspension up to 10^-3.
Perform a spread plate using 50 μL of the 10^-3 diluted suspension on an MH agar plate.
Incubate the plate overnight (∼14 h) at 37°C under micro-aerophilic conditions.
Count the colonies that appeared on the plate.
Grow monolayers of human INT407 cells in the presence of coverslips in a 6-well tissue culture plate (1.2×10^6 cells/well).
Incubate C. jejuni cells for 1 h with DAPI (40 μg/mL) in the dark before infection.
Add C. jejuni at MOI 300:1 to the INT407 cell monolayers.
Incubate the mixture for 3 h at 5% CO2 and 37°C in DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS.
Remove the culture medium after incubation.
Wash the cells with 500 μL/well of 1× PBS.
Treat the cells with 150 μg/mL of gentamicin (total volume up to 500 μL/well) for 2 h.
Wash the cells three times with 500 μL of 1× PBS.
Mount the coverslips using 5 μL Vecta-shield mounting media for fixing.
Use a DAPI filter with an excitation wavelength of 300–450 nm and an emission wavelength of 380–650 nm to visualize invaded C. jejuni cells.
Grow monolayer of human INT407 cells in 24-well tissue culture plate (3 × 10^5 cells/well).
Add C. jejuni at MOI 300:1 when the cells become 70% confluent.
Incubate for 5 h at 5% CO2 and 37°C in DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS.
Remove the culture media after incubation.
Wash the cells with 500 μL of 1× PBS three times.
Add 300 μL TrizoL reagent to detach the cells by vigorous pipetting.
Transfer the solution into a 1.5 mL micro-centrifuge tube at room temperature (∼25°C) for 20–30 min.
Isolate RNA and prepare cDNA as mentioned earlier (Sub-step 14; c–m).
Amplify the C. jejuni 16S rRNA gene from the cDNA using PCR cycling conditions.
Run equal volume of the PCR product on a 1% agarose gel.
Quantify the band intensity using ImageLab software.
Amplify the hcp gene using an equal volume of cDNA.
Run equal volume of the PCR product on a 1% agarose gel.
Quantify the band intensity using ImageLab software.
